question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+{e}^{t}\,k$ for $t\in [\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ]?$
question.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=5\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)={e}^{t}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,k \\  & =-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+{e}^{t}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }(y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }25{cos}^{2}⁡t-25{sin}^{2}⁡t+{e}^{2t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }25\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+{e}^{2t}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$
